MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L2·N4786unmasked layer
This neuron's output is uniformly negative, reaching its maximum (least-suppressed) value on sentence-final periods (including "." followed by a newline) that close a paragraph/statement, and its most extreme negative value on the `<|begin_of_text|>` token and ordinary document-opening words — i.e., it's essentially a "start-of-document vs. sentence-boundary" polarity signal rather than a semantic detector.

This neuron gives its (small) positive peaks on highly predictable "glue" tokens mid-phrase in flowing descriptive prose — prepositions ("of", "in"), a comma in a list, and past participles/verbs completing a noun phrase ("led by", "was had", "were covered") — rather than on content words, which (nouns/adjectives in technical or legal text) drive it strongly negative.
